clue.text: Not quite hang on, faced with hard chance

definitions.note: to chance is to come about by luck, a verb

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to hang something on is to append it

explanation.surface: Someone clinging on, up against something hard, leaving things to luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced with' means the hard letter goes in front; 'Not quite' signals the last letter of the phrase's synonym is dropped. 'chance' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance and to occur are both verbs for something coming about by luck.

clue.text: Prime minister's residence

definitions.meaning: Sir Alec Douglas-... was British prime minister 1963-64
the place where one lives, one's house

explanation.surface: Where the prime minister lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling place is a house where one lives; separately, Alec Douglas-Home was a twentieth-century British premier.

clue.text: Powerful emotion as one goes in to die

indicators.note: goes in signals that one piece is put inside the phrase for dying

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Intense feeling as someone enters their final moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'die' is a two-word euphemism, so the numeral splits it between its words. 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong feeling such as love or rage is a classic sense of the word; also Christ's suffering.

clue.text: Some units upset almost falling over …

indicators.note: falling over signals the whole string is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: SI units are the international system of scientific units

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: upset as in knocked over, of a drink: spilled

explanation.surface: A set of measures knocked over and nearly toppling, trailing off into dots.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the three dots at the end of the clue, which also lead into 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission or a trailing-off are called by this punctuation name.

clue.text: Waste food? Rudely, the police are going to

parts.note: pigs is a rude slang term for the police
will expresses the future, like are going to

explanation.surface: A rude remark about officers on their way to collect leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes slops fed to swine.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps fed to swine are literally waste food.

clue.text: … useless, 15, consumed with vice

indicators.note: consumed, as if eaten and churned up, signals that the letters are mixed together

parts.note: the number written out as a word gives these letters

explanation.surface: Continuing from 3 down: someone pointless at fifteen, eaten up with bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' here is the number spelt out, FIFTEEN, not a cross-reference; with VICE its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no effect is of no use, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Material examples of second team on board

parts.note: a watch is a team of sailors on duty aboard ship

explanation.surface: Fabric samples from a reserve side of players on a ship or committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like a committee; it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cut samples of cloth shown to customers are fabric samples of this name.

clue.text: Check long note coming from one I serve

indicators.note: coming from says the other pieces follow on after the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A servant checking a sustained musical tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is German, the motto of the Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Wales's German motto translates as a pledge of service.

clue.text: Troublingly, an allergy affecting part of the throat

indicators.note: troublingly suggests the letters are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: An allergy is causing trouble in someone's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what relates to the voice box, a part of the throat.

clue.text: I regret in the morning having knocked back something spicy

indicators.note: knocked back, as of a drink, signals the string is read backwards

parts.note: alas expresses regret
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Regretting a morning after downing a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: ALASAM read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spice mix used in South Asian cooking, as in garam masala.

clue.text: Satisfied with top mark for speaking? Don't take that literally

parts.note: met as in satisfied, of a demand
A is the highest grade

indicators.note: speaking means the word is to be taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: the word for, said out loud

explanation.surface: A pupil pleased with a top grade for an oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: PHOR is how 'for' would be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech is a non-literal usage, so the warning against literal reading describes it.

clue.text: For holiday, books trip for one, strangely wearing suit

indicators.note: wearing means the suit goes round the other letters like clothing

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters are put in an odd new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker books a solo trip, oddly wearing a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns TRIPFORI into IRPORTFI, which 'wearing' puts inside ACTION after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Light paperback novels bought at terminals for holiday reading form this genre.

clue.text: Charging along a stretch of tarmac?

definitions.text: Charging along a stretch of tarmac?

parts.words: Charging along a stretch of tarmac?
parts.note: seems to be about speeding down a highway; in fact charging means levying fees for its use

explanation.surface: Someone racing down a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' means billing motorists, not rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Levying tolls on drivers for using particular highways is the policy name.

clue.text: Begging to fix prison in Arctic

parts.note: to mend is to fix

indicators.note: in places the jail inside the cold word

parts.note: arctic means icy, freezing
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Pleading to repair a jail in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the practice of living by asking alms, which is begging.

clue.text: Chap is admitting "restorative" means "hand jobs"

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: admitting means the short word lets the remedy inside it

parts.note: a cure is a restorative remedy

explanation.surface: A man defends a restorative as meaning something cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy-looking definition is innocent: treatments for the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty treatments of the fingernails are literally jobs done on hands.

clue.text: Anxious to put forward name for bender

indicators.note: put forward means the named letter is shifted nearer the front

parts.note: keen as in eager, anxious to do something

explanation.surface: Eager to nominate someone for a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' looks like a binge; it is a joint that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg joint is something that flexes, hence a whimsical bender.

clue.text: A reduction of weight, drinking always juice

indicators.note: drinking means the shortened word takes the other inside it
reduction of means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: a load is a weight carried
ever means always

explanation.surface: Cutting weight by always drinking juice.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAD loses its D to LOA, which takes in EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The gel from a succulent plant is sold as a soothing juice.

clue.text: Writers wrong to hold book back

indicators.note: back signals the whole string is read in reverse
to hold means the word contains the letter

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Authors wrongly withholding a book.
explanation.walkthrough: SBIN read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen points are the bits that write, so they are writers in a crossword sense.

clue.text: Rich? No travelling by British Airways

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about

explanation.surface: A wealthy person refusing to fly with Britain's flag carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Airways' looks like one name; 'British' gives B and 'Airways' is the definition. 'by' places B beside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The two branches of the windpipe are passages carrying air into the lungs.

clue.text: Ev-en, sort of flat?

parts.note: the word even broken in two by a hyphen is a split version of a word meaning even

explanation.surface: A puzzling hyphenated word presented as a kind of apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Even means level; the hyphen splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling on staggered floors is a kind of apartment.

clue.text: Extremely arrogant, uprooting unknown plant

indicators.note: uprooting means the letter is pulled out

parts.note: extremely means very
Y is a mathematical unknown
vain means conceited, arrogant

explanation.surface: A haughty gardener digging up a mystery plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena, a herb of folk medicine, is the plant named.

clue.text: Official room to feed horse

indicators.note: to feed means one piece is put into the other

parts.note: a foal is a young horse

explanation.surface: Space set aside for feeding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Official and ceremonious both describe things done by proper procedure.

clue.text: False emotion from which actors recoiled in play

indicators.note: in play means the letters are moving about freely and rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors shrinking from fake feelings on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping, as reptiles were fabled to do, is a show of sham sorrow.

clue.text: Makes fun of people's appearance on radio

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a guise is the outward appearance someone takes on

explanation.surface: A radio presenter mocking how others look.
explanation.walkthrough: Guise and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule them, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: In park with German, order to renew vows

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a park
OM is the Order of Merit
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A couple in a park with a German friend arranging a vow renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge oneself again is to commit anew, as in renewing vows.

clue.text: Strange phenomenon of second sight?

parts.note: second sight here is seeing something a second time, the feeling of having already seen it

explanation.surface: A spooky clairvoyant gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Second sight usually means clairvoyance; here it is a sense of seeing again.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for the eerie sense of familiarity means already seen.

clue.text: Waste small space for writing, wrongly filled

indicators.note: filled means the page takes the other piece inside

parts.note: a page is space to write on
ill means wrongly, badly

explanation.surface: Wasting a scrap of paper by filling it in badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that has slopped over is waste, lost material.

clue.text: Mass, part of it for saint

parts.note: the Agnus Dei is a part of the Mass

explanation.surface: A section of the Mass dedicated to a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to Mass: the Agnus Dei is a section of the liturgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Magnus is the patron saint of Orkney, with a cathedral in Kirkwall.
